sections.overview: Erythrodiplax gomesi is a Brazilian dragonfly first described from Pirassununga, São Paulo. A 2023 survey recorded it for the first time in Minas Gerais.
sections.identification: The taxonomic sources confirm the accepted species name and its placement among libellulid dragonflies, but the brief online records reviewed do not provide a usable field diagnosis.
sections.habitat: The 2023 Minas Gerais record came from Sempre-Vivas National Park, a highland landscape containing Cerrado, gallery forest and rocky-field vegetation; the paper does not assign the species to one of those habitats.
sections.diet: The cited species records provide no prey information specific to Erythrodiplax gomesi.
sections.behavior: The 2023 park inventory records the species but gives no species-specific behavioral details.
sections.reproduction: The cited records give no species-specific breeding information.
sections.ecology: A recent Brazilian inventory calls it a generalist that is often overlooked in collections, while also emphasizing persistent gaps in South American odonate distribution data.
sections.conservation: GBIF currently displays the global IUCN category Data Deficient. Brazil’s 2014 national assessment listed Least Concern; the scopes and dates differ.
